programmes.d: A clue no bigger than a thumbtack leads investigators to a trio of killers.
In the 1990s, the media dubbed Richard Rogers the "Last Call Killer" because he targeted men in gay bars who were obviously intoxicated.
In 1995, Palm Beach waitress Denise O'Neill is abducted and murdered.
While investigating the apparent overdose suicide of Reverend Bill Guthrie's wife, detectives recover incriminating files from Bill's computer and learn of his infidelity.
A young girl with no ID is found on an isolated farm but has mailbox and house keys.

On September 17, 1984, in a suburb of Tucson, Arizona, eight-year-old Vicki Hoskins left home on her pink bicycle to mail a letter for her mother. She never returned, but her slightly damaged bicycle was found nearby.
A woman disappears without a trace, along with two others who vanished under similar circumstances.
When two boys are brutally attacked, investigators rely on evidence fished out of a nearby pond. It became the first case where diatom analysis was used to place a suspect at the scene of the crime.
In 2003, St. Cloud teenager Jason MacLennan returned home and discovered his father Ken's body.

A twelve-year-old girl claimed she had been abducted and sexually assaulted. She recounted what happened in such a flat, unemotional voice that police found it difficult to believe her. Fibers on her clothing would prove she was telling the truth.
Children die at an alarming rate at a Texas hospital, and one nurse may be involved.
This episode documents a deadly bombing at a church in Oakwood, Illinois, in December 1997.
A vacuum-cleaner bag of microscopic paint-particles helps to identify a killer.
The medical examiner ruled the death an accident, but the detectives investigating the case thought the evidence at the scene indicated otherwise.
A search in Virginia's DNA databank reveals the identity of a news producer's murderer.
A young woman attends evening church services, then disappears. When her abandoned car is found, the tank is empty and a gas can she kept in her trunk for emergencies is missing.
A man is gunned down and his wife injured. But then revealed that the wounds are self-inflicted.
Residents were stunned to learn that their bank had been robbed and the bank president was missing.

On Christmas Eve 2005, a man's body is found burning near Baltimore. He's eventually identified as 26-year-old Wesley Person. Distinctive building materials from the 1930s play a crucial role in solving this case.
When police doubt a young girl's story about being abused, fibers on her clothes help her case.

Rachael Mullenix, 19, was convicted of stabbing her mother, Barbara Mullenix, in 2006. She allegedly packed her mother's bloodied corpse in a cardboard box before dumping it in California's Newport Bay.
Shortly after daybreak in Vancouver, British Columbia, a fire was set in a dumpster.
It would take 46 years, handwriting analysis and new fingerprint technology to solve the 1957 murders of two California police officers.
An obscure style of rope and forensic analysis lead to the arrest and conviction of a murderer.
One warm summer afternoon, the town of Verona, Wisconsin faced its first triple homicide. To solve the case, investigators had to delve into the world of high rollers and offshore betting.
The body of a young woman was found a mile from her abandoned car.

One morning in a deserted area outside of Phoenix, a motorcyclist discovers the body of a young woman. She had been beaten, bound, strangled and possibly raped. Nearby plants tell investigators more about the killer.
Two eyewitnesses may hold the key to the death of a motorcycle gang member.
Witnesses saw a woman in the back of a truck, flailing her arms and screaming. When they found a jacket near a pool of blood, they knew what they had seen wasn't a joy ride.
An Ohio woman and her two daughters go missing while vacationing in Florida.
A murder trail turned cold, until police got a call from a woman whose husband, Gerald Powers, had a criminal past and a fondness for Chevy Berettas.
A death in Pennsylvania is strikingly similar to one in North Carolina.

When police find the body of 11-year-old Krista Harrison, there are few clues to the killer's identity. But authorities are intrigued by unusual orange fibers embedded in clothing found near the victim.
19-year-old Lori Auker left her Pennsylvania home for work and never arrived.

The investigation into the kidnapping and rape of an 18-year-old Ohio woman is aided when the victim returns hours after the incident occurred. With her help, the police are able to track the assailant to his front door.
A young woman suddenly becomes critically ill, eventually leaving her unable to walk.
In 2007, Shamaia Smith disappears from a strip club in East Hartford, CT. Police consider various patrons of the club, but focus on local businessman Kenneth Otto.
A man states that a robber shot his wife, but a song he downloaded makes investigators suspicious.
When two women went missing and were later found brutally murdered, police wondered if they were victims of a hate crime.
Tara Munsey went missing after a work shift at a Virginia restaurant.

When heart surgeon Darryl Sutorius is found dead in the basement of his upscale Cincinnati home, police assume he committed suicide. Further investigation reveals that his new wife Della has a history of violence and an insatiable desire for money.
Lack of evidence compels investigators to look beyond the obvious when a woman is beaten to death.
On October 15, 1985, two bomb explosions rocked Salt Lake City and resulted in two deaths. A third explosion occurred the next day; this time, the victim survived.
Fingerprints found at the crime scene helped investigators to apprehend a killer.

There was no clear reason for a young, healthy college student to be dead. But when the coroner discovered a tiny clue during the autopsy, investigators were able to uncover a mystery filled with betrayal and revenge.
When a policeman's house goes up in flames, experts suspect arson. But then the suspect vanishes.

In 1990, Shirley Andronowich's body was found mutilated. Eyewitnesses told police she had a fight with her husband the night before, but forensic evidence proved that he had nothing to do with her death.
A man becomes the prime suspect when his parents are killed in a house fire.

Firefighters find an entire family dead inside their home in an apparent murder-suicide, but there are several inconsistent clues in the rubble. Could ballistics, a time card and some secret audiotapes unravel the mystery?
Two suspects are linked to a murder by bloodstained boots and a gun.

In 1996, Derrick Duehren returned to find his Oregon home burned to the ground. His wife's charred remains were later found in the rubble. Investigators set out to determine if it was an unfortunate accident or murder.
Crystal Faye Todd's case is examined; the popular high school student was raped and murdered.
On May 12, 1994, Crystal Perry was viciously murdered in her home in Bridgton, Maine. Michael Hutchinson, 32, was later found guilty in the slaying.
When a wealthy socialite died after falling down the stairs, witness accounts contradicted evidence.
A victim's knowledge of forensic evidence leads police to her abductor.
In 2005, the body of young mother Summer Baldwin was found in a suitcase in a Texas landfill.
A convicted arsonist claims his innocence and sets out to prove it.

A mysterious computer crash pushed a thriving manufacturing company to the brink of collapse, jeopardizing hundreds of jobs. Forensic investigators had to determine if the crash was the result of a computer defect, human error, or sabotage.
A woman's diary helps police piece together the events surrounding her murder.
In 1987, the death of Crystal Purcell was considered an accident. Then in 2001, Barbara Purcell called police to suggest that her estranged husband had killed Crystal.
A two-man shrimp boat sinks when a fast-moving, violent storm strikes the Louisiana coast.

Three seemingly unrelated deaths prove to be serial murders. The killer had been careful; he used poison which had no taste or odor. Fortunately for investigators, it also had a unique chemical signature.
When the wife of a well-known dentist is found dead, police struggle to identify a suspect.
After the 1996 murder of Seattle residents Raquel Rivera and Jay Johnson, evidence from the couple's dog eventually ties one of the murderers to the scene.

A 6-year-old girl ran and hid when she saw her grandmother being beaten to death, but the man followed, beat and assaulted her. She said the assailant was her uncle, who was later convicted. She recanted her testimony years later.
In 1995, police in San Diego, California are baffled by a pair of hands found in a dumpster.

A wealthy man and his wife were attacked by three masked men outside their luxurious Louisiana home. He was shot dead and she was forced to open their hidden safe. To solve the crime, police would have to find out who knew about the concealed safe.
An assistant manager of a Florida steakhouse is stabbed to death.
Ten bodies had been found between May and November 1984 in Florida.

A suspicious fire sweeps through an apartment, killing two young women. The cause of the fire and the identity of the victims are unclear, but a closer look at the scene reveals something hidden in the ashes.
In 1995, the founder of American Atheists disappeared with $500,000 in gold coins.
Faced with three homicides that appear to be professional executions, investigators on both sides of the Atlantic must find a common thread between the victims.
A man disappears one year to the day after beginning an affair with his friend's wife.
In 1987, a human skull and some bones were discovered at a Boy Scout Camp near Farmington, Missouri. Facial reconstruction aids the investigators in this case.
Highway policeman is shocked when a bloody traffic collision is classified as an accident.

Police suspect Dr. John "Jack" Boyle in the disappearance of his wife, Noreen, when he signs mortgage papers for a new house with a woman pretending to be his spouse. The police later find Noreen's body in the basement of Dr. Boyle's new house.
In 1993, worldwide attention focused on robberies which targeted tourists in Florida.

An investigation of a pediatrician, prompted by the mysterious death of one of her patients, leads to a Texas hospital where the pediatric mortality rate is higher than at any hospital in the country.
Investigators sift through the ashes of a fire which killed a 40-year-old woman.

A young woman was found dead on a golf course in the Bahamas. The grass on that course was so distinctive, it had evidentiary value. The evidence led police to two suspects, each of whom blamed the other.
With a long list of suspects, forensic experts agree that the killer in this crime knew his victim.

It was the single most deadly automobile accident in American history. Almost a hundred vehicles were involved, twelve people died and more than fifty people were injured. And it happened along a stretch of highway long known for dense, thick fog.
Forensic psychiatry helps a wife to remember the details of how her husband was shot.

In rural Canada, Dr. John Schneeberger is accused of sedating and sexually assaulting one of his female patients and his step daughter. DNA tests demonstrate that the doctor is innocent, but the patient insists that he sedated and raped her.
At a murder scene, investigators find a shoe-print, several foreign hairs and unknown fingerprints.

Susie Mowbray was charged in her husband's death. Her son was so convinced of her innocence that he enrolled in law school, studied all of the evidence and, eventually, discovered the truth of what really happened between his parents.
The murder of a couple puzzles investigators until the victims' dog leads police to the killer.

A woman's death in Pennsylvania triggers a homicide investigation into another woman's death in North Carolina. Faced with striking similarities, examiners must determine if their suspect's story about accidental drowning is all wet.
After a man dies in a fire, his death is ruled an accident until forensic science is used.
In 1999, 9-year-old Valiree Jackson vanished on her way to school near Spokane. Her father, Brad Jackson, reported the disappearance and the entire community started searching for her abductor.
After a weekend retreat, a Boy Scout's organs start shutting down, leaving doctors puzzled.
In 1981, New York correctional officer Donna Payant disappeared and was later found in a landfill. The medical examiner not only identified the cause of death, but also found an important clue.
A postcard incriminates a high religious figure with crimes committed during World War II.

Fire engulfs the home where Lori Keidel and her siblings were left alone while their father went to the laundromat. Years after her mother's disappearance, Lori tells police she witnessed her mother's death.
A teen's role in a high school production of "Hamlet" exposes the truth behind her father's death.
When a successful stockbroker doesn't return home after a late shift, his wife reports him missing.
In 2003, Kathy Lorick was murdered on a Concord, California jogging trail in the middle of the day.
After a Philadelphia Convention, 180 Legionnaires contract pneumonia-like symptoms and 29 of them die. The determination of one scientist helps identify the cause of this deadly disease.
A flu-like epidemic spreads throughout a Navajo reservation in 1983.
